claims.text: NbMoTaWVTi is an example of the proposed refractory high-entropy alloy family.
The feedstock can have controlled O, N, and C interstitial impurity levels.
Avoiding elements with very large oxide-formation enthalpies will prevent oxide precipitation.
The proposed refractory alloy family can be fabricated by PBF-LB/M without high-temperature build-platform heating.
Rapid solution annealing after PBF-LB/M will homogenize the microstructure.
Rapid solution annealing will relieve residual stresses and reduce dislocation density.
Rapid cooling can kinetically retain a high-temperature phase in NbMoTaWVTi-related material.
Rapid PBF-LB/M cooling minimizes diffusion time and thereby suppresses Laves-phase and other intermetallic precipitation.
Cr and Si can promote brittle intermetallic compounds in refractory high-entropy alloys, with Cr promoting Laves-phase precipitation.
Rapid annealing can relieve residual stresses without permitting grain-boundary segregation of embrittling impurities.
Suppressing Laves phases and controlling grain-boundary chemistry will maintain a metastable or single-phase BCC solid solution.
PBF-LB/M processing can introduce high dislocation density.
The proposed process will produce a homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure without brittle grain-boundary precipitates.
The proposed microstructure will provide superior high-temperature strength and ductility relative to conventionally processed or slowly cooled material.
Silicides, B2 phases, and Laves phases in refractory high-entropy alloys are intrinsically brittle and are associated with limited ambient-temperature tensile ductility.
Intermetallic compounds can form at grain boundaries and cause brittleness in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Conventional casting or slow cooling typically causes grain-boundary Laves, silicide, or B2 formation and poor high-temperature structural integrity.
TiO has an FCC structure at elevated temperature and a monoclinic structure at ambient temperature, creating a cooling-rate-related phase-stability concern in NbMoTaWVTi.
The critical cooling rate needed to suppress Laves-phase formation in the proposed Group IV-V alloy systems is unknown.
Thermal processing alone may be insufficient to mitigate interstitial-impurity embrittlement without prior powder purification.

contradictions.description: The alloy is labeled as a Group IV-V transition-metal family, but the listed NbMoTaWVTi example includes Mo and W, which are Group VI elements.

The rapid anneal is said to relieve or reduce dislocation density, while the final material is predicted to retain high dislocation density; the hypothesis does not explain how much density remains after annealing.
